page.overview:
Who is Blucher von Vincke?

Blucher von Vincke was a grandmarshall of the Imperial Army who is renowned as the writer of The Empire at War, a book about five important battles fought by the soldiers of the Empire of Man during its long history.

The book was printed with the blessing of Emperor Karl Franz by the Altdorf Press in 2523 IC.

In his time, von Vincke commanded many different armies: peasant levies armed with staves and scythes, mercenaries from Tilea and Estalia, professional gunners from Nuln, Halflings, Reiksguard knights, regiments of professional spearmen and Empire Greatswords. He recounted how these troops came from all of the Empire's different states, from all walks of life, and were inhibited by all the natural distrusts and prejudices held against anyone not from their home village, town or city. Yet von Vincke managed to forge all of them into cohesive, disciplined armies, and he claimed to have done it by providing a common goal and instilling a pride in their hearts for the army they served in, just as Sigmar did before him.

During his military career, Grandmarshall von Vincke suffered a resounding defeat in Tilea, one that ruined his career, for thereafter his reputation was forever tainted. That fiasco was mentioned in the grandmarshall's book, but the excuse he claimed for the defeat was that he had been hampered by freak storms and several mercenary companies that changed sides in the midst of the battle.
